ORDERED TO THIRD READING RULES CAL.557

items.actClause: AN ACT authorizing the county of Saratoga to effectuate a lot line adjustment involving a portion of reforested lands in the town of Moreau
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5626

TITLE OF BILL:

An act authorizing the county of Saratoga to effectuate a lot line
adjustment involving a portion of reforested lands in the town of
Moreau

PURPOSE:

To allow the county of Saratoga to complete an equitable transfer of
real property with the Saratoga County Water Authority (SCWA) in order
to make improvements and upgrades to SCWA's water treatment plant.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 allows the county of Saratoga, acting by and through the
county board of supervisors, to effectuate a lot line adjustment
involving a portion of reforested lands described in section two.

Section 2 describes the real property to be conveyed by the county of
Saratoga pursuant to section one.

Section 3 describes the real property to be acquired by the county and
dedicated for reforestation purposes, and conditions the authorization
in section one upon an equal acreage transfer of real property from
the Saratoga County Water Authority.

Section 4 states the effective date and the law this bill amends.

JUSTIFICATION:

In 2008, the county of Saratoga conveyed to the SCWA a 21.86 acre
parcel of county owned reforested land for the construction of a water
treatment plant. Because the county conveyed the reforested parcel to
SCWA for a purpose other than reforestation or one authorized by
County Law § 219, the county sought and obtained home rule legislation
under Chapter 439 of the Laws of the 2006. SCWA subsequently
constructed the water treatment plant and all necessary appurtenances.

Recently, in the course of designing needed improvements and upgrades
to its water treatment plant, SCWA discovered that portions of the
water treatment facility, as constructed, enter onto adjoining
reforested lands of the county. In order to remedy SCWA's entry onto
the county's reforested lands, the county and SCWA have proposed an
equitable transfer of real property between the two entities: (1) the
westerly boundary of SCWA's parcel is expanded by 5 acres onto land
currently owned by the county and (2) the southern boundary of SCWA's
parcel is reduced by 5 acres, with the property restored to county
ownership and re-designated as county reforested land.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:


None to the State.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.
